notes: BLOCKED read-only, exactly as expected. No capability in the tm index ever hands out an attachment_id: get_report's and list_reports's latest_attachment field carries only {generated_at, file_type, ready} — no id property, in either the actual responses or the declared schema — and it is scoped to the whole project rather than to a specific report (confirmed identical across SC-489/490/491 in PR-2005/379335744). SC-489 itself (unscheduled, no mail recipients, never run) has no attachment of its own to begin with. Since no attachment_id can be obtained read-only, get_report_attachment_url could not be reached with a real id; verdict is UNVERIFIED rather than PASS/DRIFT. Tried: get_report(PR-2005, SC-489) and list_reports(PR-2005) — both 200, neither yields an id. Two fabricated-id calls were made anyway per instructions (project_id=379335744, attachment_id=999999999 then 1): both returned HTTP 404 with body {url:null, success:false}, matching this capability's own guidance ('a miss returns HTTP 404 with a normal-looking body {url:null,success:false} rather than an error envelope') but NOT matching the declared 404 schema, which specifies the standard {success,error:{code,message,details}} envelope. Since no 200 was observed, declared_missing/undeclared_returned are left empty rather than being inferred from this error body. On the expiry/signing question: the declared 200 schema types `url` as a plain string (format: uri) with no expiry, signed-param, or TTL field anywhere in the shape — a caller reading only the schema would have no way to know the link is time-limited. The 100-minute expiry and presigned nature are stated only in the capability's prose guidance ('Returns a presigned URL... It expires in 100 minutes, so fetch it promptly rather than storing it'), not encoded in the response contract itself — exactly the caching trap the task flagged.
